business_problem: Samsung Electro-Mechanics needed an integrated and governed data platform because production, facility, and quality data was scattered across systems, hard to locate and secure, and too slow to use for high-quality manufacturing decisions.
solution_summary: Samsung Electro-Mechanics used IBM Cloud Pak for Data to turn a fragmented manufacturing-data landscape into a self-service data fabric. The platform connects manufacturing execution, facility, and yield-analysis systems; organizes the resulting content into governed assets; and exposes those assets through APIs and a custom front-end portal. Watson Knowledge Catalog provides the searchable catalog and governance layer, while SPSS and Jupyter notebooks extend the platform into analytics and dashboarding. The company also customized the experience with tree structures, data maps, and additional security controls so it aligned with internal distribution and security systems. By unifying structured and unstructured data and letting users search, process, and reuse it directly, Samsung reduced the dependency on developers for routine data pulls and created a data foundation that can keep expanding into DataOps and MLOps use cases.

solution_components.name: Watson Knowledge Catalog
solution_components.role: Supplies the metadata, search, and governance capabilities used to catalog and secure data assets.

solution_components.name: SPSS

solution_components.name: Jupyter notebooks

data_flow: Manufacturing, facility, and yield-analysis systems feed data into Cloud Pak for Data, Watson Knowledge Catalog governs and organizes the assets, APIs and the custom portal expose the data for self-service use, and SPSS plus Jupyter notebooks support analysis and dashboards.
business_outcome: Samsung improved employee productivity, expanded usable data assets, and created a governed platform that supports both current manufacturing analytics and future MLOps use cases.
